data.body_html:
Planning a stag do in Marbella and wondering about the marbella boat rental stag weekend cost for 2029? You're in the right place. With prices starting at €749 for two hours on an Astondoa 40 – all inclusive – a private boat charter is often cheaper than a VIP club table and way more memorable. This breakdown covers exact pricing, hidden costs, and budget tips so you can plan without surprises.

Real Pricing: What You Actually Pay

We operate two pricing tiers for stag groups. Tier A covers the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) at €749 for 2 hours up to €2,299 for 8 hours. Tier B is the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) from €4,719 for a minimum 4 hours, which includes a free jet ski. All other boats (e.g. Ferretti 94, Canados 86) are priced on request via WhatsApp – we don't list them here because rates vary by season. Every price includes the licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance and 21% Spanish VAT. No hidden marina fees or cleaning charges.

Per-Person Cost: The Stag Math

For a group of 10 on the Azimut 39, the 8-hour charter costs €2,299, which is €230 per person. Compare that to a night out in Puerto Banús where a bottle in a club can cost €200–€400. You get a full day on the water with unlimited drinks, a skipper to handle navigation, and stops at coves like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. For the Mangusta 80, split 12 ways: €4,719 ÷ 12 = €393 per person for 4 hours including a jet ski session. That's competitive with a high-end dinner and drinks.

Budget Tips for 2029

  • Book shoulder season: May, September and October offer lower prices and fewer crowds. You'll still get 25°C+ sea temperatures and sunny skies.
  • Choose a 4-hour slot: For most stag groups, 4 hours is enough time to cruise to Cabopino, swim, and enjoy lunch. It's cheaper than a full day and avoids fatigue.
  • Bring your own food: While we provide snacks and drinks, you can bring a catered platter (order through us from €15/person) or your own picnic. No corkage fee.
  • Share the cost upfront: Use a payment app to collect from each guest before the charter. This avoids awkward chasing on the day.
  • Avoid add-ons: Jet skis are included with the Mangusta 80, but for other boats, you can add a jet ski for around €150/hour. Decide if the group really wants it.

What's Included (No Surprises)

Every charter from Boat Rental Marbella includes: a licensed English-speaking skipper, fuel for the day, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, full insurance, safety equipment, and 21% Spanish VAT. The skipper will also act as host – pointing out landmarks like La Concha mountain, the Golden Mile villas, and the best spots for swimming. You don't tip the skipper, but if service is excellent, 10–15% of the charter fee is appreciated.

Which Boat Fits Your Stag Group?

For groups of 9–11, the Azimut 39 or Astondoa 40 are ideal – both depart from Puerto Banús and offer a spacious cockpit, sun pads, and a cabin for changing. For 12 people, the Mangusta 80 (or its grey sister) gives you 24m of deck space, a flybridge, and a free jet ski. If you want something different, the Fairline Targa 12m (10 pax) or Pershing 46 (10 pax) are sporty options – just message us for pricing.

Typical Stag Itinerary: 4-Hour Sample

Most groups depart around 11:00 from Puerto Banús. Head west past the luxury homes of the Golden Mile, then drop anchor at Cala del Faro for swimming and lunch. After a couple of hours, cruise to Cabopino beach for a quick stop, then back to port by 15:00. That leaves the evening free for dinner at a chiringuito or a club in Banús. If you book 8 hours, you can go as far as Estepona or even Sotogrande for a longer swim stop.
